title: The government's own fraud report never mentions immigrants
body: For more than a year the Trump administration has told the same story. Immigrants are draining healthcare dollars and driving up costs by defrauding the government. The Intercept reports that Health and Human Services' own inspector general just released a semiannual report on healthcare fraud, and immigrants don't appear in it once. What does appear is corporate executives. One CEO ran a scheme pushing medically unnecessary devices on Medicare patients. An insurance broker built an Affordable Care Act scam that preyed on homeless people and people fighting addiction. The National Health Care Anti-Fraud Association puts the total cost of healthcare fraud as high as $300 billion a year, most of it providers billing for services never rendered.

The rhetoric points the other way. In May, JD Vance warned of "tens of billions" going to "illegal aliens" in California. Mehmet Oz, the TV doctor now running Medicare and Medicaid, blamed "immigration-related costs." Stephen Miller said the budget would balance if benefits only went to people "lawfully correctly eligible." Meanwhile Trump pardoned Lawrence Duran, who got 50 years for a $205 million Medicare scheme. The California governor's office found Trump's pardons erased nearly $2 billion owed back to taxpayers and fraud victims.
So the people running the biggest scams are getting clemency, and the people who commit the least fraud are getting raided. That isn't an accident. It's the plan.
